#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Zero-token merge-tail patrol. Run by pr-babysit.timer (or manually).
#
# For every open bead labeled merge-when-green with a PR external ref:
#   - PR merged/closed upstream        -> close/annotate the bead
#   - checks pending                   -> wait (do nothing)
#   - checks green + base branch green -> merge (method from bead notes), close bead
#   - checks failed, no rerun yet      -> rerun failed jobs once (if allowed), mark it
#   - checks failed after rerun        -> relabel merge-blocked, unclaim, so the bead
#                                         surfaces in `bd ready` for an agent to judge
#
# Design: sessions produce (review/fix/push + scripts/pr-handoff), this patrol alone
# consumes (merge/close). bd claims cannot distinguish two sessions of the same user,
# so mutual exclusion comes from this role split, not from claims.
#
# Zero model tokens; safe under cron; flock-guarded; bd calls are serial.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/pr-babysit"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
LOG="$STATE_DIR/patrol.log"
LOCK="$STATE_DIR/lock"

exec 9>"$LOCK"
flock -n 9 || exit 0   # another patrol run is active

log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }

cd "$ROOT"

QUEUE="$(bd list --label merge-when-green --json 2>/dev/null)" || { log "bd unavailable (lock/migration gate?); skipping run"; exit 0; }
COUNT="$(jq 'length' <<<"$QUEUE")"
[[ "$COUNT" == "0" || -z "$COUNT" ]] && exit 0

log "patrol start: $COUNT queued bead(s)"

jq -c '.[]' <<<"$QUEUE" | while read -r item; do
  bead="$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$item")"
  ref="$(jq -r '.external_ref // ""' <<<"$item")"
  notes="$(jq -r '.notes // ""' <<<"$item")"

  # Accept both conventions: gh-pr-<n> (default repo) and gh:owner/repo#<n>.
  repo="gastownhall/beads"; pr=""
  if [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh-pr-([0-9]+)$ ]]; then
    pr="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  elif [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh:([^#]+)#([0-9]+)$ ]]; then
    repo="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; pr="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
  else
    log "$bead: unparseable external_ref '$ref'; skipping"
    continue
  fi

  state="$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json state --jq '.state' 2>/dev/null)"
  case "$state" in
    MERGED)
      bd close "$bead" --reason "PR $repo#$pr merged (observed by pr-babysit)." >/dev/null 2>&1
      log "$bead: $repo#$pr already merged; bead closed"
      continue ;;
    CLOSED)
      bd update "$bead" --remove-label merge-when-green \
        --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] PR closed unmerged upstream; needs a decision." >/dev/null 2>&1
      log "$bead: $repo#$pr closed unmerged; label removed"
      continue ;;
    OPEN) ;;
    *)
      log "$bead: cannot read $repo#$pr state; skipping"
      continue ;;
  esac

  checks="$(gh pr checks "$pr" --repo "$repo" 2>/dev/null)"
  pend="$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="pending"' <<<"$checks" | wc -l)"
  fail="$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="fail"' <<<"$checks" | wc -l)"

  if [[ "$pend" -gt 0 ]]; then
    log "$bead: $repo#$pr waiting ($pend pending, $fail failed)"
    continue
  fi

  if [[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]]; then
    # Base-branch health gate (stop-the-line rule) before merging.
    if ! PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE=1 "$ROOT/bd-main/scripts/pr-preflight.sh" "$pr" --repo "$repo" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
      log "$bead: $repo#$pr green but preflight blocked; leaving for agent judgment"
      bd update "$bead" --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] checks green but preflight blocked (red base or policy); see patrol.log." >/dev/null 2>&1
      continue
    fi
    method="squash"
    [[ "$notes" == *"method=merge"* ]] && method="merge"
    [[ "$notes" == *"method=rebase"* ]] && method="rebase"
    if gh pr merge "$pr" --repo "$repo" "--$method" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
      bd close "$bead" --reason "PR $repo#$pr merged by pr-babysit ($method) after green checks + preflight." >/dev/null 2>&1
      log "$bead: MERGED $repo#$pr ($method); bead closed"
    else
      bd update "$bead" --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] merge attempt failed (branch protection / review requirement?); see patrol.log." >/dev/null 2>&1
      log "$bead: merge of $repo#$pr FAILED; noted on bead"
    fi
    continue
  fi

  # Failures present.
  if [[ "$notes" != *"flake-rerun-done"* && "$notes" == *"flake_rerun=allowed"* ]]; then
    runs="$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="fail" {print $4}' <<<"$checks" | grep -oE '/runs/[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | sort -u)"
    for rid in $runs; do
      gh run rerun "$rid" --repo "$repo" --failed >>"$LOG" 2>&1 && log "$bead: reran failed jobs of run $rid"
    done
    bd update "$bead" --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] flake-rerun-done: reran failed jobs of run(s) $(tr '\n' ' ' <<<"$runs")." >/dev/null 2>&1
  else
    bd update "$bead" --remove-label merge-when-green --add-label merge-blocked \
      --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] checks still failing after rerun budget; needs agent judgment. Failing: $(awk -F'\t' '$2=="fail" {print $1}' <<<"$checks" | tr '\n' '; ')" >/dev/null 2>&1
    bd unclaim "$bead" >/dev/null 2>&1
    log "$bead: $repo#$pr BLOCKED (persistent failures); relabeled merge-blocked + unclaimed"
  fi
done

log "patrol end"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hand a PR's merge tail to the pr-babysit patrol instead of watching CI in-session.
#
# Creates-or-claims the tracking bead for the PR, labels it merge-when-green,
# and records the merge policy in the bead notes. The pr-babysit timer (see
# scripts/pr-babysit) then owns the merge: sessions that run this script must
# NOT merge, close, or re-run checks on the PR afterwards.
#
# Usage: scripts/pr-handoff <pr-number> [--repo owner/repo] [--method squash|merge|rebase] [--no-flake-rerun] [--bead <id>]
#
# When several beads share the PR's external ref (e.g. a tracking bead plus a
# follow-ups bead), pass --bead to name the merge-tail bead explicitly; the
# ref lookup otherwise takes the first match.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
REPO="gastownhall/beads"
METHOD="squash"
FLAKE_RERUN="allowed"
PR=""
BEAD_OVERRIDE=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) REPO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --method) METHOD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --bead) BEAD_OVERRIDE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-flake-rerun) FLAKE_RERUN="no"; shift ;;
    -*) echo "unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *) PR="$1"; shift ;;
  esac
done
[[ -n "$PR" ]] || { echo "usage: pr-handoff <pr-number> [--repo owner/repo] [--method m] [--no-flake-rerun]" >&2; exit 2; }

cd "$ROOT"

title="$(gh pr view "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --json title,state --jq '.title')" || { echo "cannot read PR $PR on $REPO" >&2; exit 1; }

# Find an existing bead under either external-ref convention.
bead="$BEAD_OVERRIDE"
[[ -n "$bead" ]] || bead="$(bd list --json --external-ref "gh-pr-$PR" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[0].id // empty')"
[[ -n "$bead" ]] || bead="$(bd list --json --external-ref "gh:$REPO#$PR" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[0].id // empty')"

if [[ -z "$bead" ]]; then
  bead="$(bd create --title="$title" \
    --description="Upstream PR: https://github.com/$REPO/pull/$PR — merge tail handed to pr-babysit patrol." \
    --type=task --priority=2 --external-ref="gh:$REPO#$PR" --json | jq -r '.id // .[0].id')"
  echo "created bead $bead"
fi

bd update "$bead" --claim --add-label merge-when-green \
  --append-notes "[pr-handoff $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] repo=$REPO pr=$PR method=$METHOD flake_rerun=$FLAKE_RERUN — patrol owns the merge; sessions hands off here." >/dev/null

echo "handed off: $REPO#$PR -> bead $bead (label merge-when-green, method=$METHOD, flake_rerun=$FLAKE_RERUN)"
if ! systemctl --user is-active --quiet pr-babysit.timer 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "WARNING: pr-babysit.timer is not active. Enable with: scripts/install-pr-babysit" >&2
fi

base_runs=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$base_ref" --status completed \

# to run last cannot mask a red test workflow (and vice versa).

  | [.[] | select((.conclusion // "") == "success" or ((.conclusion // "") | test("^(failure|timed_out|action_required)$")))][0]
  | select(. != null)]' <<<"${base_runs:-[]}")

base_green_count=$(jq '[.[] | select(.conclusion == "success")] | length' <<<"$base_latest_per_wf")

Check failures on this PR may be pre-existing base breakage, and merging onto a red base hides new failures. Merge only the fix for ${base_ref} while it is red; for everything else wait, then update the branch and re-run checks."

  ((.conclusion // "") | test("FAILURE|CANCELLED|TIMED_OUT|ACTION_REQUIRED")) or
  ((.state // "") | test("ERROR|FAILURE"))
)] | length' <<<"$json")

  if (.status? // null) != null then
    .status != "COMPLETED"
  elif (.state? // null) != null then
    (.state | test("^(EXPECTED|PENDING)$"))
  else
    true
  end
)] | length' <<<"$json")

  block "$failed_checks status check(s) failed or require action."
elif [[ "$pending_checks" -gt 0 ]]; then
  block "$pending_checks status check(s) are still pending."
else
  pass "No failed or pending status checks reported."
fi

if [[ "$beads_files" -gt 0 ]]; then

fi

test_files=$(jq '[.files[]?.path | select(test("(^|/)(test|tests)/|_test\\.go$|\\.bats$"))] | length' <<<"$json")

fi

  warn "Large PR; verify scope is one issue and one PR."
fi

I like it a lot. The architecture is right: agents produce and hand off; one zero-token patrol owns merging. That directly solves the same-user Beads claim race.

I’d call it an excellent v0.1, but not yet a fully trusted merge controller. The main hardening gaps are:

- Pin the reviewed head SHA with `gh pr merge --match-head-commit`. Currently a push between preflight and merge could change what gets merged.
- Verify the PR is actually `MERGED` before closing the bead. `gh pr merge` can succeed after merely entering a merge queue.
- Replace note-string configuration with typed Beads metadata. Historical `method=...` and `flake-rerun-done` strings can affect later handoffs incorrectly.
- Make blocked-state updates idempotent. PR #4702 has accumulated 50+ identical notes, producing a 164 KB patrol log in under a day.
- Parse `gh pr checks --json` and fail closed on command/data errors.
- Add state-machine tests with fake `gh` and `bd`; currently syntax passes and ShellCheck only finds the unguarded `cd`, but there are no behavioral tests.
- Give the systemd service a finite timeout and generate its checkout path instead of hardcoding `%h/dev/mybd`.

The strongest parts are the `flock`, serial Beads operations, red-base preflight, bounded flake retry, and explicit escalation to `merge-blocked`. The timer is active and it has already successfully merged a real PR, so the idea is validated.

My verdict: keep it and make it standard—but harden head pinning, post-merge verification, and state storage before treating it as unattended infrastructure. See [pr-babysit](/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/scripts/pr-babysit:71) and [pr-handoff](/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/scripts/pr-handoff:39).

---
title: Issue Metadata
description: Storing arbitrary JSON on issues as the extension point for integrations and execution hints
---

The `metadata` field on issues accepts arbitrary JSON. Any valid JSON value is stored as-is.

Metadata is the preferred extension point for data that is specific to an
integration, orchestrator, team workflow, or experimental automation. Before
adding first-class fields, commands, or schema changes, check the
[Project Charter](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/engdocs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md#schema-boundary).

## Example: Agent Execution Metadata

Agent execution hints are one example of using metadata to extend beads without
adding new native database fields. Automation may store these hints so agents
can make routing decisions without parsing prose. Agents enacting an issue
should read metadata first, then use description and notes for scope and
rationale:

```bash
bd show <id> --json | jq '.[0] | {id,title,metadata,description,notes}'
```

The current convention for execution hint keys is:

| Key | Meaning |
|-----|---------|
| `execution_agent_type` | Suggested worker class, such as `explorer`, `worker`, or `mixed`. |
| `execution_suggested_model` | Suggested model for the parent agent or spawned subagent. |
| `execution_reasoning_effort` | Suggested reasoning effort, such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh`. |
| `execution_mode` | Whether work should be local, delegated, or staged between delegated and local execution. |
| `execution_parallel_group` | Grouping hint for work that can run alongside related tasks. |

These keys are advisory metadata, not core issue fields. When a workflow uses
them, they take precedence over free-form notes for execution routing. Notes
remain useful for rationale, ownership, and exact prompts.

Model and effort values are portable hints, not runtime bindings. The
`execution_reasoning_effort` values above are a canonical advisory scale:
writers should store canonical values rather than runtime-local ones, and a
consumer whose runtime uses a different scale should map the stored value to
its nearest native level instead of dropping the hint. Likewise,
`execution_suggested_model` is a capability-tier suggestion: a consumer on a
different provider should substitute a model of the same tier rather than
ignore the hint.

Parent/orchestrator agents must consume these keys before spawning subagents.
Model and reasoning effort are normally fixed at launch, so reading metadata
after delegation is too late.

Do not add a first-class helper such as `bd show <id> --execution` or
`bd plan <id> --json`. Issue gh-3541 resolved to keep execution hints as
metadata only; the JSON/JQ snippet remains the supported access path.

## Example: Tracker Round-Trip Metadata

Tracker integrations map external issues into beads fields such as title,
status, priority, type, labels, dependencies, and `external_ref`. When an
integration needs to preserve tracker-specific fields that do not belong in the
native beads schema, it can store those fields in issue metadata:

```json
{
  "example_tracker": {
    "board_id": "ENG",
    "sprint_id": 42,
    "remote_type": "story"
  }
}
```

This keeps beads' core issue model stable while allowing the integration to
round-trip fields it understands. Prefer namespaced keys and keep
tracker-specific policy in the integration. If a value becomes broadly useful
to beads itself, revisit whether it deserves a native field.

## Reserved Key Prefixes

| Prefix | Reserved For |
|--------|------------|
| `bd:` | Beads internal use |
| `_` | Internal/private keys |

Avoid these prefixes in user-defined keys to prevent conflicts with future Beads features.

- [Project Charter](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/engdocs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) - Product scope and schema boundary
- [#1416](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/1416) - Optional schema enforcement (future)
